ev.q: Among these 26 persons, 23 (88%) experienced an illness meeting the case definition; illness onset date was available for 20 persons
Characteristics of illness and exposure to swimming pool water — hotel A, Maine, March 2023
Among the 23 patients, 16 (70%) had ear pain, 15 (65%) had a rash
Among 35 guests who responded, 23 (66%) developed ear pain, rash, or pain or swelling in feet or hands within days of using the pool
illness began a median of 24 hours (range = 8 hours–6 days) after use of the hotel A pool

public_health_question.v: What caused the outbreak of ear pain, rash and hand-foot pain among guests who used a Maine hotel swimming pool in March 2023, and what contributed to it?

ev.q: The outbreak was caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa . Inadequate maintenance and monitoring of chlorine concentration likely contributed to this outbreak.
Pseudomonas Infection Outbreak Associated with a Hotel Swimming Pool — Maine, March 2023
Maine CDC initiated an epidemiologic, laboratory, and environmental health investigation.
interviewed a representative from each household using a standard questionnaire

equity.level_reason: Only age and sex of cases are described, with no group-specific outcomes or social-position framing.

ev.q: age ranged from 5 months to 61 years (median = 8 years)

notes: Attack rate among pool users (23/26) is reported but not compared with non-users, so the cluster is read as a descriptive case series (limited). Pool-log compliance counts and SNP relatedness are case-confirmation or inspection steps, not comparisons. Discussion figures on 1971–2021 outbreaks are cited from a previous report.
view_issues: The Abstract gives 23 of 35 respondents (66%) as cases, while the text gives 23 of 26 pool users (88%); both are consistent but use different denominators.
